Once upon a time, there lived a grumpy old man. Every day he would grow more and more angry. One day, he had had enough. He grabbed a big clock from the wall and marched outside with it.

The old man sat down and began to chew on the clock. He felt very angry and he wanted to take his anger out on the clock. He chewed and chewed, until finally the clock was no more than just a few pieces of metal.

When the old man had finished, he looked around and noticed a tired-looking, little girl sitting nearby. The girl had been watching him the whole time but she hadn't said a word.

The old man smiled and said, "What a calmyou are!" The girl smiled back, but then she looked at the destroyed clock and gasped in horror.

The old man had forgotten he was holding the clock and he felt embarrassed. He quickly said goodbye to the little girl and ran away. He never wanted to be reminded of what he had done.

The moral of the story is to not let your anger take control of you.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to go outside and explore her neighborhood. One day she wandered into a big park and noticed a friendly old man. He smiled and asked her if she wanted to hear a story.

The girl said yes, excitedly. He smiled and whispered: â€œOnce upon a time there was a brave knight who carried a bow. He was gentle, kind and compassionate. He used his bow to protect the people in his kingdom and they were very grateful.

The man then asked the little girl, â€œDo you know what the most important thing was to the brave knight?â€

The little girl shook her head. â€œItâ€™s his compassion. He was able to show kindness to everyone and help make the kingdom a better place.â€ 

The man smiled warmly and the little girl thanked him for the story. She went home feeling inspired and determined to be kind like the brave knight, who never stopped using his bow and showing compassion to everyone.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Sarah and Tony, who loved to go for walks in their town. One day, they wanted to explore a part of town they hadn't seen before. They had to choose which way to go. There was a beautiful creek with a bridge that crossed over it or a dark, mysterious forest. 

Tony chose the creek and they headed towards the bridge. It was a beautiful walk and they found a lot of new things to explore. But when they reached the bridge, they stopped. It looked old and dangerous, and they weren't sure if it was safe to cross. 

Sarah stopped and thought for a moment. She said to Tony, "Let's not cross it, Tony. It looks too dangerous. Let's find another way."

Tony realized Sarah was right, and they chose the safe option. They found a nicer, safer bridge to cross, and they safely made it to the other side of the creek and found some wonderful things to explore.

The moral of the story is that it is important to choose the safe option, even if it is not the most exciting. Taking chances can be dangerous and it is better to make wise choices.

Once upon a time, there lived a strong little giraffe. He had a dream to leave his home and explore, so one day he packed his things and set off.

He soon arrived at a great lake, but he had no way of crossing it. Just then, a nice hippo came along and said, "I can help you cross. Just hop onto my back!"

The giraffe was so happy and hopped onto the hippo's back. As they swam across the lake, the hippo said, "In the middle of the lake, you'll need to grab the pole so we can keep swimming straight."

The giraffe grabbed the pole with his strong hooves and kept steady as the hippo continued to swim. Soon they made it to the other side, and they both said goodbye and went their separate ways.

The giraffe was so grateful for the help of the hippo and continued his journey feeling stronger than ever. In the end, he achieved his dream and left to explore the world.

Once upon a time, there was a pig and a sheep who were good friends. One day they decided to go on an adventure and went to a fountain in the middle of a forest. The pig said to the sheep, "Look, let's feed the fountain some food." The sheep asked, "What have we got to feed it?" The pig thought for a moment and said, "Let's find some hairy fruit!"

So the two friends began looking for food. They found lots of hairy fruits and wanted to feed the fountain. They threw all the fruit into the fountain but nothing happened. The fountain was still dry. The two friends went back to the fountain and the sheep said, "Maybe we need to feed the fountain more than just food." 

The pig replied, "You are right! Let's put some of our love into the fountain too." So they both held hands, put their hearts and souls into the fountain and said, "Let our love feed the fountain."

Suddenly, the fountain burst out with the clearest water they had ever seen! They quickly filled their buckets and brought it back to their home.

The moral of this story is that when you give love you also receive it. We need to fill our hearts with love and share it with others.

John had his own paint. He was very excited and happy to show it to his mom. He said, "Mommy, I own paint!" His mom replied, "That's great John, let's paint together!" So, they opened the paint and John started to draw with it.

After a while, John finished his masterpiece and it looked so beautiful to him. He said to his mom, "Look mommy, I own tight paint!"

His mom was surprised and said, "Wow John, that's very impressive. Let's hang it up!" But, before they could hang the painting, John had an accident and the paint got smeared all over the place. His mom tried to console him but John was devastated and sad. 

The bad ending had been foreshadowed ever since John opened his paint; his mom had warned him several times to be careful and not play around with the paint too much. But, inevitably, he went against his mother's advice and it cost him dearly in the end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who lived in a small house in the country. She had a beautiful yellow blanket that her grandma had given her. She loved to snuggle up in it and take it with her everywhere.

One day, she was taking a nap in her bedroom with her blanket over her. Suddenly, she heard a sound coming from outside her window. It sounded like ruffling and rustling. She got up and looked, and saw a little mouse digging around in the garden. She said, â€œHey, little mouse, why are you disturbing my nap?â€

The mouse looked up at her and said, â€œI just wanted to find something to wrap myself up in so I could take a nice nap. Do you think you could let me borrow your blanket?â€

The little girl thought about it for a moment, and then said, â€œSure, I donâ€™t mind. Here, you can have my blanket. Just be careful with it, itâ€™s very little.â€

The mouse thanked her, and with her blanket covering her, it quickly ran away into the night. The little girl was glad she could help the mouse, and she went back to sleep, feeling warm and cozy in her little blanket.

Once upon a time there was an island. It was a beautiful and sunny place. On the island there was a big bell, and the bell would always ring. 

One day a little girl named Lucy heard the bell ringing. "What's that?" She said, "It sounds so nice!"

Suddenly, a parrot came flying down from the sky and landed on Lucy's shoulder. "That bell," said the Parrot, "is a magical bell. If you touch it, it will take you anywhere you want to go!"

Lucy was so excited and so she touched the bell. Immediately, she found herself on a beautiful tropical island. It was so wonderful! Everywhere she looked were amazing things to see.

After exploring the island, Lucy found a nice restaurant with a wonderful smell coming from it. She decided to go inside to check it out. 
 Inside, Lucy found a spicy stew that smelled heavenly. She could hardly wait to try it!

Lucy took a big spoonful of the stew and tasted it. It was so delicious! From then on, that little island was always known as Lucy's Island because of its amazing and spicy stew.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who lived at the beach. Every day, she would take a bucket and shovel and build a sandcastle. She loved to watch the giant waves crashing against it. One day, she decided to build an extra big sandcastle!

As she was making it, a shark swam towards her. The girl screamed and ran away from the shark. But then, it swam up to her and said, "Don't be scared! I just want to help you build your sandcastle!"

The girl was still afraid, but the shark said, "I'm a friendly shark! I won't hurt you, I promise!" So the girl reached into her pocket and pulled out a little open bag of sand. She sprinkled it over the sandcastle and the shark used his tail to spread it around. Together, they built a beautiful sandcastle.

The girl and her new friend said goodbye and, as the waves gently washed away the sandcastle at the end of the day, the girl was happy knowing that she and the friendly shark had built something wonderful together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Grace. Grace was obedient and always did what the grown-ups told her. Her parents were so proud of little Grace.

One day, Grace and her parents had to go to the lawyer. Grace didn't understand why, but she knew it was important, and she was still obedient.

At the lawyer, Grace's parents said that someone had broken the law. Grace didn't understand what the law was, but she could tell this was something serious.

The lawyer said that if everyone was obedient, they could try to fix the problem. Grace was so good, her parents gave her a hug, as if they were proud of her.

Grace didn't understand completely what was happening, but she knew something was about to change. Her parents were doing everything they could to make sure the law was followed. 

The lawyer and her parents worked hard to make sure that justice was served. In the end, the law was obeyed, and it was because of Grace's obedience. 

The moral of the story is that being obedient is good.

Tommy and Julie were in the kitchen with their mom. They were making dinner. 
"What are we doing, Mommy?" Tommy asked.
"We're making dinner. We are going to mix the beef together," said Mommy. She pointed to the bowl with the beef inside. 
Julie frowned. "I don't wanna mix the beef. It looks miserable!"
Tommy laughed. "Don't worry, Julie. We're just making dinner!"
Mommy smiled. "That's right. Now we need to mix it all together."
So Tommy and Julie mixed the beef together. When they were done, Mommy said, "Now we have dinner ready!"
Tommy and Julie smiled. They had made dinner and it was delicious!

As they walked along the path, Daisy saw a collar lying on the ground. She excitedly pointed it out to her mum, who paused and said, "Let's have a look at this collar, Daisy".

Once upon a time, two friends were walking through the woods. It was getting dark and it was getting scary. Suddenly the two friends heard a noise. It sounded like something was rising.

The two friends looked around and saw a card lying on the ground. It was glowing in the dark. One of the friends was brave and decided to pick it up. But when they touched it, the card began to rise.

The two friends were scared. They backed away slowly. The card kept rising until it stopped moving.

The brave friend stepped forward and said, "What are you?"

The card opened up and out floated a magical butterfly.

The two friends were so happy. The butterfly fluttered around them and then flew away. The friends learn that there was nothing to be scared of.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Emma. Outside, the sky was grey and gloomy. Emma was feeling sad.

"What can I do?" Emma said.

Suddenly, a bright light appeared in the sky. It was the sun, rising slowly into the air. Emma smiled.

"Let's go outside and play," said Emma.

So, Emma and her father went outside. The sun was shining and it was a beautiful day. Emma ran around in the grass and enjoyed the warm sunshine.

Emma's dad said, "It sure is nice to see the sun again. I'm so glad it's a beautiful day."

Emma giggled and said, "Me too!"

They stayed outside until the sun set in the sky. The sky was still gloomy, but Emma was happy.

Once there was a pink shape. It was a nice shape and it kept growing. Every day the shape increased.

One day, a boy saw the shape and tried to touch it. The shape got angry and said, "Don't touch me!" The boy was scared and ran.

The boy told his mom what had happened. His mom said, "Maybe you should have been more friendly. Even though the shape was scary, it didn't mean you had to be scared too."

The next day, the shape had increased even more. The boy was curious, so he decided to try again. This time, he said, "Hi. I'm very sorry for being scared yesterday. Can I look at you?"

But before the shape could reply, it started to grow bigger and bigger until it was too big for the boy to handle. He ran away, scared.

Moral: Be friendly even to those who appear scary.

Once upon a time, there lived a small, fearful mouse in a cozy little house. One night, the mouse saw something glowing through the window. It was so bright and warm. It made the mouse feel curious and brave.

The mouse opened the window and saw a cocoa tree full of bright, twinkling lights. He crept closer and saw the lights were stars. The mouse was amazed!

Suddenly, he heard a kind voice call out to him, "Do you want to come and play with me?" The mouse thought it was the stars speaking. He was afraid, but also wanted to play. He said, "Yes!"

The mouse hopped out the window and the stars twinkled brighter. The mouse knew he was safe and wanted to stay with the stars forever. He welcomed their warm glow and the sweet smell of cocoa in the air.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Alice. She loved to go on adventures! Her favorite thing was to get her passport and check out different places around the world.

One day, Alice asked her mom if she could get her passport and go on an adventure. But her mom was feeling a bit grumpy and said no.
Alice was very unhappy and started to cry. "What did I do wrong?" she asked.

Alice's mom looked at her with a smile and said, "That's okay my darling. You can still have an adventure, just not with a passport. I can tell you a story about a far away place that would be fun for you to explore!"

Alice nodded her head and smiled. Soon, she was off exploring this magical world her mom had told her about. She had an amazing time, and realized that sometimes even without a passport you can still have a great adventure!

One day, Oliver went to the backyard with his mom. He saw a big hole in the ground. His mom said, "We need to bury this here". He didn't know what it meant.

Oliver watched as his mom put the big thing into the hole. Then she started to fill it with dirt. He asked, "What is it, mommy?"

She said, "It's an old chimney. We have to take it out so we can build a new one." She looked frustrated.

The next day, when Oliver went back to the backyard, the big hole was gone. He said, "Mommy, I can't find the chimney!"

His mom smiled and said, "We buried it!"

Once, there was a dry pony. He wanted to work, but he was too weak.

He said to his owner, "Please, let me work. I can do it!"

But the owner said, "No, you are too weak. You can't do it!"

The pony was sad but he kept on trying to work.

He tried and tried and he worked hard, but he still couldn't do it.

One day, the dry pony got too sick. He wasn't able to work and he had to be put to sleep.

The end.

One morning, Jack woke up feeling excited. He sensed something was different. 

Jack asked his mum, "Mum, what is today?" 

His mum replied, "Today is a special day, Jack. We are going to measure the dead tree in the backyard!" 

Jack was so happy he jumped up and down. He asked, "How will we measure it?" 

His mum said, "We will measure it with a tape measure. We will measure the height and width of the tree!"

Jack enjoyed measuring the dead tree. He stretched out the long tape measure from the top of the tree trunk to the ground, and then around the trunk. In the end, Jack was proud of the measurements he made on that special morning!

Once upon a time, there were two friends - a kitten and a puppy. They were playing in the park together when the puppy stopped suddenly. He said to the kitten, "Look, do you see this perfect tree?" The kitten looked up and saw a tall tree with leaves of many colours. He nodded his head. He agreed with the puppy, the tree was perfect.

The puppy then jumped and said in a loud voice, "Let's climb the tree!" The kitten starred at the puppy and shook his head. He had never climbed a tree before and didn't think it was a good idea. But then, the puppy smiled and said, "It's be fun! I'll show you how." So, the two friends started climbing the tree together.

It was hard work, but with the puppy's help, the kitten made it to the top of the tree. He was so proud of himself and looked out over the park. He turned to the puppy and smiled. Then, they both nodded their heads in agreement - it was the perfect view.

One day, Mommy and Johnny went to the park. They saw a tall grass and Mommy decided to cook it. Johnny was so excited and watched as Mommy picked the grass. 

Mommy found a mysterious pot and put the grass in it. Then she added a few unknown ingredients. Johnny stared in amazement as it smelled so good. 

Mommy lit the fire and stirred the pot. She continued to stir and stir until the grass was cooked. Johnny was so excited!
 
Mommy served the tasty grass for dinner and both Mommy and Johnny loved it. They laughed and smiled as they enjoyed their yummy dinner.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was walking down a path. She came across a surprise, a pretty, shiny jewel! The girl was so excited and asked, "What is it?" 

The jewel started to move and spoke to the girl. It said, "I am a magical jewel and will grant you three wishes!"

The girl was amazed and asked, "Can I keep you?" The jewel revealed that it wanted to stay with the girl forever.

The girl embraced the jewel and said, "I wish we could be best friends forever!"

The jewel smiled and said, "Your wish is granted!" The girl was so happy that she now had a magical jewel friend who was always with her.

From that day on, the little girl and the jewel were always together. Everywhere the girl went, the pretty jewel went too. They were the best of friends forever!

Once upon a time there was a girl named Carla who loved to catch bugs. She would catch all kinds of creepy crawly bugs in the garden. One day she noticed a bright blue bug and she decided she wanted to catch it. She ran around and around the garden but the bug was too fast! She chased the bug until she was all out of breath.

Suddenly, a big white napkin landed on the blue bug! Carla cautiously picked the napkin up and carefully opened it; and there it was, a beautiful blue bug! She was so excited! 

Carla sat in the garden to enjoy her catch. But soon, she realized that it wasn't as exciting as she thought it was going to be. She looked around for something else to do but all she could find was an old, boring tree.

Carla approached the tree and asked, "Hey, tree. Do you have anything fun to do?"

The tree said, "I may not look like it, but I'm full of surprises. Come and take a closer look and see what you can catch!" 

Carla was delighted and soon she was collecting leaves and petals, she made herself a colourful crown, and she even caught a butterfly! She had a great time exploring the tree and the garden with her new found treasures.

Once upon a time there was a rabbit and a mouse who were good friends. The rabbit was always very careful and thought before she moved. The mouse, who was very foolish, was always in a hurry and didn't think before he moved.

One day, the rabbit and mouse were walking along and saw a cactus. The mouse saw the cactus and was very excited. He quickly moved and touched it. But, to his surprise, he felt a sharp prick! He screamed in pain.

The rabbit quickly ran to the mouse. The rabbit said, "You're so foolish! Why did you move so fast? You should have thought before you moved. Always use caution when touching something you're not familiar with."

The mouse learned his lesson and was more careful after that. He thought before he moved and never made the same mistake again. Since then, the mouse and the rabbit had a great time exploring their new world. They never forgot the moral of their story: it is important to think before you move.

Once there was a cheerful little boy called Ben. He loved to ride in the elevator. Every time he did, he would be so excited he couldn't help but make funny noises.

One morning, Ben was in the elevator with his Grandma. As they reached the top floor, Ben pressed the button to open the doors. "Ahchoo!" he sneezed.

Grandma smiled. "Bless you, Ben," she said. She looked at him, with a gleam in her eye. "You must be feeling very cheerful."

Ben smiled back, before dancing out of the elevator. They were going to have a fun day together, and he couldn't wait!

Once there was a chubby little girl named Jane. Jane wanted very badly to learn how to play the piano. Every day she heard the piano music coming from her neighbor's house, and it made her want to learn even more. However, her parents did not permit her to learn. They said she was too young and it was too expensive.

Jane was determined to change her parents' minds, so she hatched a plan. She practiced very hard on an old piano that was in her grandmother's attic. When her parents came to visit, she asked them if she could play them a song. To Jane's surprise, they said yes!

As Jane played, her parents were so amazed. They finally let her take piano lessons. Jane was so happy that she could finally learn how to play the piano she had been dreaming about.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Jack who lived with his Mommy and Daddy. He was very happy but he sometimes worried about things. 

One day, Jack was watching TV when Daddy suddenly said: "Hey Jack! Can you help me make breakfast?" Jack was so excited. He loved helping Daddy do things.

So Jack said "this one is brilliant!". Daddy smiled and said: "You're right Jack! That's the one I was going to pick too!". 

Jack was so proud of himself. He had made the right choice and he knew it. Daddy gave him a big hug and they had a wonderful breakfast together. From then on, Jack never worried about making decisions - he knew he was brilliant!

Once upon a time, there lived a family of four. Every morning, the family would pay the man to take care of their house. One morning, something happened that shocked the family.

"Mommy, outside there's lots of smoke!" said the 3 year old. The family was surprised and went to the windows to have a look.

Outside, they saw the smoke from a dead tree. "Let's pay the man to take care of this!" said the father. 

So the family paid the man to chop down the tree and take away the smoke. 

But the family soon realised they had a problem. The man was too tired and fell asleep!

They all started laughing and waited for the man to wake up. When he did, the man worked hard to take care of the tree and soon the smoke was all gone. 

The family was happy again and thanked the man for his work. 

The end.

Once upon a time there was a little squirrel who wanted to pick a leaf. He scrambled up a tall tree and reached out his tiny paw to grab the leaf. But he was too stupid and instead of picking the leaf he dropped it. The little squirrel looked down and got very sad. The leaf floated away in the wind and he wanted it back.

Then, a big wise owl swooped down from the sky. He asked the squirrel, â€œWhy are you so sad?â€

The squirrel told the owl what happened and admitted, "I dropped the leaf".

The wise owl said, â€œThatâ€™s okay. You just need to be more careful next time. And donâ€™t be so stupid.â€

The little squirrel thought about the wise owlâ€™s advice and learned to be extra careful before he picked up anything again.

The moral of the story is: be careful and don't be too stupid!

Once upon a time, there was a small cub and his name was Ben. Ben was always curious and he wanted to peek around. One day, he decided to peek inside a cave. As he looked into the cave, he saw a lion inside! He was very scared, but the lion was very big and hot.

"Please don't be scared," said the lion. "I won't hurt you. I'm just here to help you." 

Ben was a little bit relieved, but he was still scared. He wanted to run away and hide. 

"I understand," said the lion. "Let me give you some advice. Always think before you peek. If something looks scary then it may be too dangerous to take a look."

The lion got up and vanished into the forest. Ben was very relieved, but also sad that the lion had gone. He thought about what the lion had said and decided that he would always think before he peeked. 

The moral of the story is that it's ok to be curious, but always be careful and think before you peek!

Molly and her mom were in the kitchen. Molly watched as Mommy put some smelly pasta in a pot.

"Mommy, what are you doing?" asked Molly.

"I'm making us dinner," mommy said.

Molly watched in excitement as the pot boiled. Suddenly, she saw a bug on the counter.

"Mommy! Mommy! I can catch it!" Molly said, picking up the bug.

Mommy said, "That's great, Molly! Now, can you help me get the pasta out of the pot?"

Molly grabbed a spoon and carefully lifted out the pasta. She smiled as she smelled the smelly pasta.

"That smells yummy, Mommy!" Molly said.

Mommy and Molly enjoyed their dinner. As they ate, Molly thought about how she had caught the bug. She was proud that she had helped make dinner.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Max and Jane. Max was strong, while Jane was not. Max decided to show her how strong he was, and so he said he would lift a heavy bucket. Jane thought Max was silly, and so she laughed.

Max picked up the heavy bucket and carried it over to Jane. He said, "See! I'm strong enough to lift this bucket!" Jane clapped for him. She looked admiringly and said, "I wish I was as strong as you Max".

Max smiled and said, "You don't have to be strong like me. You just need to work together with your friends â€“ it's easy then!" Jane was surprised by this. She said, "That's true, Max! Working together is much easier!" 

They both laughed, gave each other a big hug, and went off be happily ever after. The moral of the story is that if you work together with others, you can do big and heavy things much more easily.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was only 3 years old. She was playing in a huge park with lots of other kids, when she saw a big path up ahead. The path was huge and meandered through the park and across the grassy fields.

The little girl wanted to follow the path, so she started walking along it. As she followed the path, she saw a big crack in the ground. The crack was so big that it made the path impossible to cross.

The little girl became very angry and sad. She asked her mom, "Mom, can you help me fix the crack in the path?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, of course I can help. I'll get your dad and he can help us fix it."

Mom and Dad brought shovels from home and started digging around the edges of the crack. After a lot of work, the crack was filled and the path was fixed.

The little girl was so happy and excited! She smiled and ran back to her friends to tell them that the path was fixed. They all rejoiced and ran along the huge path together.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a fish who lived in the ocean. He was small and independent. Every day, he liked to bathe in the warm tide.

One day, as he floated along in the sea, he heard a voice say, "Good morning!" The fish was surprised, and he turned around to see a larger fish smiling at him. 

"Where do you come from?" asked the small fish.

"I come from a place far away," answered the large fish. "I take a bath in the tide every day. Do you do the same?"

The small fish nodded. "It feels nice to bathe in the warm tide," he said.

The larger fish smiled. "Yes, it's very nice indeed," he said. "It makes me feel independent and free. I'm glad to meet you, small fish."

The small fish smiled in return. From that day on, they enjoyed swimming and bathing in the tide together.

Once there was a smart rabbit named Danny. He was always curious and loved exploring. 

One day Danny wanted to explore the big house he lived in. He hopped from room to room until he came to the bathroom. He had never been in there before and he lay down on the furry rug to take a closer look. 

Danny saw that the bathroom was very sparkly. The floor was made up of shiny little tiles and there was a bright bath in the corner. He hopped closer to take a peek and saw that the bath was filled with warm water and bubbles. 

Danny thought it looked like lots of fun and he wanted to jump in! After a few minutes of bouncing up and down, Danny finally decided to take a bath. He hopped in and lay down in the bubbly water. 

Danny enjoyed the warm water and felt so clean and smart when he got out. From then on, he loved taking baths and he always felt smart when he finished.

Polly smiled and said, â€œI love to paint! When can I do it again?â€

Ernie was playing in his room when he heard a terrible noise coming from outside. He stepped outside to investigate and he saw that his dad was out in the garden involved in a big project.
